Your mission

We have challenging tasks for you:

As a Data Platform Engineer, you will be responsible for building and evolving modern cloud platforms for Data & AI. Together with our team and our clients, you will develop platforms that can be operated in a scalable, secure, and sustainable manner.

In doing so, you will combine cloud infrastructure, platform architecture, and modern Data & AI technologies into solutions that create a stable foundation for analytics, data engineering, and AI use cases.

In detail, you will:

  • Design, build, and continuously evolve cloud-based Data & AI platforms

  • Develop platform strategies and target architectures together with our clients and implement them technically

  • Design scalable and robust platform architectures that serve as a foundation for data-driven solutions

  • Provision modern cloud infrastructures on Azure or AWS automatically using Infrastructure as Code

  • Work specifically with Terraform or OpenTofu as well as modern CI/CD processes

  • Design and evolve Databricks platforms regarding workspaces, compute, networking, identity, security, and governance

  • Support data, analytics, and AI teams by providing stable and high-performance platforms

  • Contribute to technical concepts, architecture workshops, and the further development of our standards together with our team


Your profile

What we are looking for

You work in a structured manner, think in terms of platforms and architectures, and implement technical solutions cleanly and sustainably.

Ideally, you bring to the table:

  • Sound experience in building modern cloud infrastructures and platform architectures

  • Excellent knowledge of at least one cloud platform, ideally Microsoft Azure or AWS

  • A strong understanding of scalable, secure, and maintainable system and platform architectures

  • Experience with technologies in the Data & AI domain, particularly Databricks

  • Knowledge in areas such as cloud networking, identity & access management, security, and governance

  • Basic software development skills, e.g., with Python, as well as experience handling APIs and automation

  • Experience with Git and CI/CD

  • A solid understanding of the requirements that data, analytics, ML, and AI workloads place on a modern platform

  • A completed degree in Computer Science, Business Informatics, or a comparable qualification

  • The ability to quickly learn new technologies and apply them purposefully

  • A structured, self-reliant, and solution-oriented way of working

  • Very good German skills (C2) and good English skills

What we would also be happy to see:

  • Experience with Databricks Unity Catalog and governance concepts

  • Experience with Azure Private Link, VNet Integration, or comparable AWS networking concepts

  • Knowledge of Azure DevOps, GitHub Actions, or comparable CI/CD solutions

  • Experience with Microsoft Fabric, Azure Data Factory, or other data platform technologies

  • Experience with Landing Zones, platform blueprints, or standardized cloud deployments

  • Experience in client projects and technical architecture workshops

  • Certifications in the context of Databricks, Azure, or AWS

Are you looking to design and build modern Data & AI platforms in the cloud and actively shape the technical future for our clients?

Do you think in terms of platforms and architectures, enjoy working hands-on with Infrastructure as Code, and want to create sustainable foundations for data and AI applications?

  • Work-Life Balance & Flexibility: We embrace flexible working models—depending on the team and department, our colleagues work hybrid or remote-only. description:
What we are building

ecoplanet builds the operating system for the energy transition. Our software helps European businesses cut energy costs, run more efficiently, and take the pain out of managing energy day to day. We are around 40 people and backed by EQT Ventures, HV Capital and others.


Why This Role Matters

You build and run the platform the whole product sits on: the event streams, the backend services and the cloud infrastructure everything else is built on. Meter readings arrive from industrial sites across Europe, through messages or us accessing APIs. Your job is to make sure that traffic lands reliably, moves through the system in a shape other teams can build on, and keeps doing so as the number of sites grows.
You join a team of 12 engineers in two squads. Small team, real ownership, and what you build reaches customers in weeks rather than quarters.

What you will work on

  • Event streaming. Kafka is the spine of the system. You own topic and schema design, partitioning, retention and delivery semantics  and the everyday reality behind them: consumers falling behind, replays, backfills, late and duplicated readings.
  • Backend services in TypeScript. The ingestion services, integrations and APIs around that stream. Every site is a little different, so a good part of the job is turning that variety into one consistent interface the product squads can rely on.
  • Cloud infrastructure on GCP. Compute, networking, IAM, infrastructure as code, CI/CD and observability. The goal is a paved road: other engineers ship and debug their own services without going through you.
  • Technical direction. You are senior enough to set it. Where we invest in the platform, what we standardise, what we deliberately leave rough for now  and bringing the rest of the team along with it.


What Sets You Up for Success

Must have:

  • At least 6–8 years building and running backend systems in production, including real time in a platform or infrastructure role that other engineers depended on
  • Strong backend engineering in TypeScript. You have designed, shipped and operated services and APIs in it — not just touched it around the edges of a frontend
  • Hands-on with Kafka in production. Topic design, consumer groups, ordering and delivery guarantees, and what you actually do at 3am when a consumer group is hours behind. A comparable streaming platform is fine if you know it at that depth
  • Solid on GCP or an equivalent cloud: containers, networking and IAM basics, infrastructure as code, CI/CD, monitoring and alerting. You have owned infrastructure, not just deployed onto it
  • Comfortable with high-volume time-series data: ingestion, data quality, backfills, and the everyday reality of late, missing and duplicated readings
  • You have seen a few things. Enough production years behind you to know which trade-offs come back to bite, when the boring option is the right one, and how to make a call with incomplete information instead of waiting for certainty
  • Kubernetes knowledge at the level of running it, not only deploying to it.
  • Clear written and spoken English. German is a plus
Nice to have:
  • Energy, industrial, IoT or another domain where the data comes off real hardware
  • Metering or device protocols, telemetry at scale, or streaming pipelines
  • Knowledge of a second programming language, like Python, Go or Kotlin
  • You run what you build: monitoring, alerting, and the occasional early morning debugging a pipeline


What You Get

  • Top-of-market team, flat hierarchy — work alongside people who push you to get better
  • Competitive salary
  • Full ownership from day one — you actively shape our company
  • Central office, easy commute — free lunch every Tuesday and Thursday
  • Wellpass membership
  • Regular 1:1s and retros focused on your growth
  • Real impact — your work supports Europe's transition to a smarter energy system

About the role

Gauss Fusion is aiming to build the first commercial scale fusion power plant based on the stellarator concept and is seeking an experienced mechanical engineer to lead on development of the robotic maintenance approach.
The fusion environment within the reactor is very aggressive, and in-vessel components such as the breeder blanket and divertor will need to be replaced on a regular basis as the materials become damaged by the radiation. Due to the environment inside the device, and in order to maintain a high overall availability, the maintenance must be done robotically using automated systems to extract and replace the components and bring the removed ones to a hot cell for separation, waste treatment, and recycling.
Gauss Fusion is looking for an innovative mechanical design engineer with experience in robotics to lead the work defining and developing the maintenance approach for the Gauss stellarator power plant and its key stellarator systems. While the magnetic configuration will be designed to maximise access to the reactor, the complex geometry poses a challenge to fixations and kinematics, and inventive approaches to the problem are required.


Main responsibilities

Manage the Gauss Fusion maintenance approach to meet the requirements of a commercial scale fusion power plant design:

  • Develop workable approaches to achieving high power plant availability, taking account of engineering and physics requirements across the reactor.
  • Integrate these remote maintenance requirements into plant layout specifications.
  • Define approaches to minimising hot cell inventory through efficient handling of removed components.
  • Lead development of the breeder blanket and divertor segmentation and fixations resulting from these approaches.
  • Lead development of remote maintenance testing and demonstration systems for the reactor.

  • Bachelor’s degree in mechanical engineering or related field, master’s or Ph.D. preferred.

Objective of the role

We're looking for an enthusiastic frontend engineer with the skills and ability to turn great ideas into reality. You should have an in-depth understanding of current web technologies and front-end development, and be passionate about creating a great user experience. Your input will help us grow and maintain our React front-end.

Join a team that encourages you to explore, learn, and go beyond, while seeing your work lead to actionable results. Put your creative problem-solving and development skills into action and make a positive impact on science and society. This is a full-time position based in Germany.


The team

You will be an integral part of the product team dedicated to enhancing ResearchGate's publisher-facing product. This role involves designing, constructing, and refining the platform to further our mission of facilitating global scientific connections and ensuring open access to research. At present, our team is working on making ResearchGate a great platform for publishers to connect with existing and future authors.

Your immediate colleagues will consist of JavaScript and PHP engineers, an Engineering Manager, a Product Manager, a UX Designer, and a UX Writer. Our team places great value on our collaborative and communicative work culture and we eagerly anticipate integrating a new Engineer into this environment.

  • Seamlessly integrate our front-end with our back-end world using GraphQL and PHP.

  • Maintain and improve existing features and related infrastructure.

  • Collaborate with Product Managers, Designers, and Software Engineers to deliver compelling publisher-facing products.

  • 5+ years frontend web development experience in TypeScript (React), CSS

  • Demonstrated ability to create code that is easily comprehensible, maintainable, and testable.

  • Approach problem-solving thoughtfully, embracing curiosity and maintaining an open-minded perspective.

  • Knowledge of GraphQL.

  • It would be a plus if you already had knowledge of relational and document-based databases (we use MongoDB and Postgres).

  • You take responsibility over your own solutions and continuously improve them.

  • You engage in proactive and efficient communication within our distributed work environment.
